items.title: 식당 광고에 AI 음식 사진 썼다가 역풍…"입맛 떨어진다"
items.summary: [지디넷코리아]미국 식당가에서 인공지능(AI)으로 만든 음식 사진을 광고에 활용하는 사례가 늘고 있다. 전문 사진 촬영보다 빠르고 저렴하게 홍보물을 만들 수 있다는 장점 때문이지만, 실제 음식과 동떨어진 이미지가 소비자들의 거부감을 불러일으키는 현상도 나타나고 있다.24일(현지시간) 월스트리트저널(WSJ)에 따르면 최근 미국에서는 테이크아웃 메뉴판부터 델리 매장 진열대까지 AI로 생성한 음식 이미지가 확산하고 있다. 전문 사진 촬영을 기다리지 않고 필요한 이미지를 빠르게 만들 수 있고 마케팅 비용
items.content:
비용·시간 절약 위해 AI 활용하는 식당 늘지만 소비자 반응 엇갈려

유통/생활/문화 입력 :2026/09/25 11:09 수정: 2026/09/25 12:29

미국 식당가에서 인공지능(AI)으로 만든 음식 사진을 광고에 활용하는 사례가 늘고 있다. 전문 사진 촬영보다 빠르고 저렴하게 홍보물을 만들 수 있다는 장점 때문이지만, 실제 음식과 동떨어진 이미지가 소비자들의 거부감을 불러일으키는 현상도 나타나고 있다.

24일(현지시간) 월스트리트저널(WSJ)에 따르면 최근 미국에서는 테이크아웃 메뉴판부터 델리 매장 진열대까지 AI로 생성한 음식 이미지가 확산하고 있다. 전문 사진 촬영을 기다리지 않고 필요한 이미지를 빠르게 만들 수 있고 마케팅 비용도 줄일 수 있어 식당들이 AI를 활용하고 있다는 설명이다.

문제는 AI가 만들어낸 음식이 실제 음식과 미묘하게 다른 모습을 보이는 경우가 적지 않다는 점이다. 이런 사진들은 식욕을 자극하기보다 오히려 불쾌감이나 거부감을 준다는 반응을 얻고 있다고 외신은 설명했다.

이 같은 현상은 AI 이미지 생성 방식과 관련이 있다. AI 연구자들은 이미지 생성 모델이 사물의 특징을 이해해 그대로 재현하기보다 학습한 데이터를 토대로 일정한 패턴을 예측해 이미지를 만들어낸다고 설명한다.

음식의 미세한 형태나 질감을 충분히 구현하지 못할 경우 AI는 단순화된 특징에 의존한다. 예를 들어 '익힌 새우는 대체로 둥글고 줄무늬가 있다'는 특징을 과도하게 적용하면 실제 새우와 달리 둥근 고리 형태의 이미지가 만들어질 수 있다.

특정 무늬를 지나치게 규칙적으로 반복하는 것도 문제로 꼽힌다. 음식 표면의 구멍이나 돌기, 줄무늬 등이 실제보다 과장되거나 일정하게 반복되면서 일부 사람에게 강한 거부감을 일으킬 수 있다. AI 특유의 매끄럽고 인위적인 질감 역시 음식 사진에서는 이질감을 키우는 요소다.

다만 AI 이미지 생성 기술 자체는 빠르게 개선되고 있다. 외신은 최근 생성형 AI 모델이 맥앤치즈나 새우 요리처럼 복잡한 음식도 실제 사진과 비슷하게 구현할 수 있는 수준으로 발전했다고 설명했다.

그럼에도 식당의 AI 이미지 활용을 둘러싼 논란은 이어질 전망이다. 음식 광고는 소비자가 실제 제공될 메뉴의 모양과 양, 재료 등을 가늠하는 수단이기도 하기 때문이다.

외신은 비용과 제작 시간을 줄일 수 있다는 AI의 장점과 실제 음식의 모습을 얼마나 정확하게 전달할 수 있느냐는 문제가 동시에 제기되고 있다고 전했다.

items.content:
성균관대 스마트 공정·소재 설계 연구실과 한국테크노돔 탐방

카테크 입력 :2026/09/25 10:30

한국타이어앤테크놀로지(한국타이어)가 권석준 성균관대 화학공학부 교수와 함께 전기차 전용 타이어 '아이온(iON)' 개발 현장을 공개했다. 내연기관과 달리 무거운 차체와 높은 토크, 정숙성에 따른 소음 문제 등 전기차 특성에 맞춰 소재·구조·가상개발 기술을 고도화하고 있다는 설명이다.

00일 업계에 따르면 한국타이어는 최근 유튜브 채널에 권 교수와 연구실 학생들이 대전 한국테크노돔을 방문한 영상을 공개했다.

권 교수는 성균관대 화학공학부와 미래에너지공학과 교수, 반도체융합공학과 겸임교수로 재직 중이다. 그는 스마트 공정 및 소재 설계 연구실을 이끌며 스마트 화학공정·소재 설계 분야의 멀티스케일·멀티피직스 모델링과 시뮬레이션, 차세대 반도체 소재·공정 등을 연구한다.

영상에는 권 교수 연구실의 박사과정생과 학부 연구생, 석박통합과정생이 동행했다. 임기원 썸머&LT 컴파운드팀장, 정문철 PCR 모델개발팀장, 김성호 버추얼 엔지니어링 담당 전무 등 한국타이어 연구진은 전기차용 타이어 개발 과정과 시험 설비를 소개했다.

탐방 중에는 한국타이어가 개발한 휠봇도 등장했다. 4개의 휠봇 모듈을 장착해 다방향 이동과 제자리 회전이 가능한 이동 장치다. 연구동에는 주행 조건에 따라 형상이 변하는 트랜스포밍 타이어 콘셉트도 전시됐다. 한국타이어는 미래 모빌리티 환경을 고려한 기술 연구도 병행하고 있다.

권 교수는 "모빌리티가 첨단을 향해 가는 상황에서 전기차는 빼놓고 얘기할 수 없는 테마"라며 "내연기관차에 맞췄던 타이어도 전기차 시대로 넘어가며 변신해야 한다"고 말했다.

한국타이어는 전기차가 배터리 탑재로 내연기관차보다 무거워지고 높은 토크를 즉각적으로 내는 만큼, 타이어에 요구되는 조건도 달라진다고 설명했다. 전기차용 타이어는 주행거리와 마모, 안전성, 소음 등을 함께 고려해야 한다는 것이다.

정 팀장은 "전기차는 배터리로 인해 무게가 늘고, 차량이 무거워질수록 타이어 마모도 빨라질 수 있다"며 "얼마나 오래 쓸 수 있는지, 차선 변경 때 무게중심이 움직여도 안전하게 운전할 수 있는지가 과거보다 더 보완돼야 할 부분"이라고 설명했다.

이어 "타이어를 단순히 두껍게 만들면 타이어 자체가 무거워지고 전비가 나빠져 주행거리가 줄어드는 문제가 생길 수 있다"며 무게와 내구성, 효율의 균형이 중요하다고 덧붙였다.

한국테크노돔에는 타이어에 가해지는 힘과 모멘트를 측정하는 플랫트랙 시험실, 소음을 분석하는 무향실, 소재 특성을 분석하는 실험실 등이 마련돼 있다. 고하중 조건과 캠버각 등을 조절해 전기차 주행 환경에 맞는 타이어 성능을 측정할 수 있다.

임기원 "고속 회전 중 타이어가 변형된 뒤 원래 형태로 복구되지 않으면 변형이 중첩돼 파장이 더 커질 수 있다"며 "아라미드가 형태를 잡아주는 데 이점이 있지만, 아라미드만 쓰면 너무 단단해지는 문제가 있어 나일론과 하이브리드 형태로 사용한다"고 말했다.

타이어 패턴 설계와 흡음재 적용을 통해서는 노면 접촉에서 발생하는 소음과 타이어 내부 공명 소음을 낮추는 방안도 연구하고 있다. 한국타이어는 접지력과 구름저항, 소음 등 상충할 수 있는 성능을 함께 조율해야 한다고 설명했다.

영상 후반부에는 가상개발 기술도 소개됐다. 실제 시험 데이터와 시뮬레이션을 결합해 개발 방향을 점검하고, 반복 제작 횟수와 개발 기간을 줄이는 방식으로 활용하고 있다고 밝혔다.

김성호 전무는 "자율주행이 들어오면 가상 타이어 자체가 실물 타이어를 대변할 수 있어야 한다"며 "타이어를 인지하는 주체가 사람에서 컴퓨터와 데이터로 바뀌게 될 것"이라고 말했다.

이어 "실제 타이어를 만들기 전 시뮬레이션과 AI를 활용해 개발 방향을 점검하면 결과물을 세네 번에 만들 일을 두 번으로 줄일 수 있다"고 밝혔다.

한국타이어는 자체 타이어 해석 프로그램 'HK-SMART'를 개발해 운영하고 있다. 향후 눈길·빙판 등 복잡한 주행 환경의 해석 역량을 높이고, 센서로 노면 상태와 마모, 하중 등을 파악하는 스마트 타이어 기술도 발전시키겠다는 계획이다.

댓글에서는 권 교수의 진행 방식과 전기차용 타이어의 필요성에 공감하는 반응이 이어졌다.

한 이용자는 "전기차가 무겁다는 것은 알았지만 타이어까지 다르게 써야 하는 줄은 몰랐다"며 "전용 타이어가 괜히 있는 게 아니었다"고 적었다. 또 다른 이용자는 "교수가 궁금한 것을 대신 물어봐 줘 더 궁금한 점이 없다"며 "어려운 내용을 쉽게 풀어 시간 가는 줄 모르고 봤다"는 반응도 나왔다.

items.title: Microsoft is killing off the ‘Copilot Plus PC’ brand
items.summary: Remember when Microsoft wanted everyone to know that "Copilot Plus PCs" were the ones to get, because those were the PCs that that'd have enough built-in AI muscle to get things done? Two and a half years later, Microsoft and Qualcomm seem to be admitting the brand is already dea
items.content:
What will Microsoft’s next buzzword be?

Remember when Microsoft wanted everyone to know that “Copilot Plus PCs” were the ones to get, because those were the PCs that that’d have enough built-in AI muscle to get things done? Two and a half years later, Microsoft and Qualcomm seem to be admitting the brand is already dead.

Windows Central ’s Zac Bowden reports that even though the new 12-inch Microsoft Surface Pro and 13-inch Surface Laptop technically meet the system requirements for a Copilot Plus PC, Microsoft is not calling them by that name anymore. “These are not called Copilot Plus PCs,” Microsoft Surface CVP Brett Ostrom told the publication.

Kedar Kondap, Qualcomm’s SVP of compute and gaming, seemed to agree that the brand’s time is done, telling Bowden that computers that offer the same experiences will “probably” not use that branding anymore.

It’s not surprising to me that Microsoft and its partners would back away. Back in 2024, smart minds pointed out that ( almost ) every PC would soon contain the basic levels of AI hardware that the brand was supposed to reflect. The flagship feature of Copilot Plus PCs, Microsoft’s Recall feature, wasn’t well received , and Microsoft took flak for constantly annoying Windows users with AI upsells, not to mention the dedicated Copilot keyboard key that you can now finally remap .

Besides, Microsoft’s flagship hardware is now about to have Nvidia chips instead , which will supposedly kick off a new era of personal AI in Windows. On October 7th , when Microsoft hosts a “conversation on how local AI will shape the next chapter of the PC,” I’m guessing it will have a shiny new brand to replace “Copilot Plus PC.”

items.content:
독일에서 변전소에 대규모 배터리저장장치를 연계해 태양광 발전 피크를 흡수하면 기존 변압기 용량의 시간대별 여유를 활용해 약 150기가와트(GW)의 태양광을 추가 설치할 수 있는 기술적 잠재력이 있다는 연구 결과가 나왔다. 기준 시나리오에서 함께 산정된 배터리 규모는 출력 약 60GW, 저장용량 240기가와트시(GWh)다.

독일 프라운호퍼 에너지경제·에너지시스템기술연구소(Fraunhofer IEE)는 독일태양광산업협회(BSW-Solar)의 의뢰로 변전소와 대규모 배터리를 결합한 태양광 추가 설치 잠재력을 분석한 단기 연구 결과를 공개했다.

연구는 고압망과 중압망을 연결하는 변전소의 변압기가 연중 최대 출력으로 가동되지 않는다는 점에 주목했다. 태양광 발전량이 급증해 변압기 용량에 근접하는 시간에는 배터리가 전력을 저장하고, 여유가 생긴 시간대에 다시 방전하면 기존 변압기 용량을 더 효율적으로 활용할 수 있다는 방식이다.

연구진은 먼저 독일 전력망에 실제 운영 중인 13개 변전소의 변압기 20대 데이터를 분석했다. 변압기 용량은 15~80메가볼트암페어(MVA)였으며, 2025년 전력수요와 기존 태양광·풍력 발전량, 전력시장 가격 등을 바탕으로 총 3040개의 연간 시뮬레이션을 수행했다.

기준 시나리오에서는 기존 재생에너지 설비와 추가 태양광의 합산 설비용량을 변압기 정격용량의 200%까지 설치하는 것으로 가정했다. 예를 들어 정격용량이 100MW인 변압기라면 기존 재생에너지와 신규 태양광을 합해 200MW 규모의 발전설비를 연결하는 방식이다.

여기에 변압기 정격용량의 40%에 해당하는 출력의 배터리를 설치하고 4시간 동안 전력을 저장할 수 있도록 했다. 배터리 왕복효율은 90%, 하루 최대 운전량은 두 차례 완전 충·방전으로 설정했다.

이 조건에서 추가 설치한 태양광 가운데 변압기 용량 한계 때문에 출력이 제한되는 발전량은 20개 변압기 평균 약 1%로 계산됐다. 배터리가 없을 경우 같은 조건의 출력제한률은 평균 약 5%였다.

연구진은 이 결과를 독일 전역으로 확대하기 위해 중·고압 전력망에 있는 변전소 3621곳을 분석했다. 이 가운데 농촌에 위치하면서 기존 재생에너지 발전 비중이 높은 1313곳을 별도 그룹으로 선정했다.

해당 변전소의 추정 변압기 용량과 기존 재생에너지 설비를 토대로 계산한 결과 약 150GW의 태양광을 추가 설치할 수 있는 기술적 잠재력이 있는 것으로 나타났다. 연구의 기준 시나리오에서는 이와 함께 약 60GW·240GWh 규모의 배터리를 적용하는 것으로 산정됐다.

150GW는 현재 독일에 설치된 전체 태양광 용량을 웃도는 규모다. 독일의 누적 태양광 설비용량은 지난 8월 128GW를 넘어섰으며, 재생에너지법에 따른 2030년 태양광 보급 목표는 215GW다.

다만 연구진은 150GW를 실제 이용 가능한 계통 접속용량으로 해석해서는 안 된다고 강조했다. 전국 1313개 변전소를 모두 시간대별로 직접 시뮬레이션한 것이 아니라 실제 분석한 20개 변압기 결과를 유사한 특성을 가진 변전소에 확대 적용한 수치이기 때문이다.

또 연구에서는 변전소보다 상·하위에 위치한 전력망의 병목이나 중압 배전망 구조를 계산하지 않았다. 태양광 설치 부지 확보와 인허가 가능성, 구체적인 사업 위치, 신규 송배전망 건설과의 경제성 비교도 포함되지 않았다.

출력제한률 약 1% 역시 전체 태양광 발전량에 대한 전국 평균 출력제한률을 의미하지 않는다. 20개 변압기에서 추가로 설치한 태양광을 대상으로 변압기 자체의 용량 때문에 발생하는 출력제한만 계산한 값으로, 전력시장 상황에 따른 출력제한이나 배터리 손실 등은 포함되지 않았다.

독일태양광산업협회는 이번 연구를 근거로 변전소 주변에 계통지원형 배터리를 확대하고 중·고압 전력망의 디지털화를 강화해야 한다고 주장하고 있다. 연구 결과대로 기존 변압기의 시간대별 여유용량을 활용하려면 태양광과 배터리, 변전소의 전력 흐름을 실시간으로 파악해 충·방전과 송전량을 함께 제어하는 체계가 필요하다.

이번 연구는 대규모 태양광 확대가 반드시 같은 비율의 변압기 증설로 이어져야 하는 것은 아니라는 가능성을 보여준다. 다만 실제 적용 여부를 판단하려면 개별 변전소의 상·하위 전력망 상태와 배터리 경제성, 부지 확보 가능성까지 포함한 현장별 계통 검토가 뒤따라야 한다.

items.content:
[스냅드래곤 서밋 2026] 프리즘ML·스펙스·엑스리얼 AR 글래스 직접 체험

반도체ㆍ디스플레이 입력 :2026/09/25 09:30

[마우이(미국)=지디넷코리아 전화평 기자] "이건 물병입니다."

안경을 쓴 채 눈앞의 사물을 바라보며 "이게 뭐야?"라고 묻자 귓가에서 즉각 답변이 나왔다. 미국 인공지능(AI) 스타트업 프리즘ML(Prism ML)이 선보인 스마트글래스가 내놓은 대답이다. 놀라운 점은 이 모든 과정이 인터넷 연결 없이 온전히 기기 내부에서 이뤄졌다는 것이다. 온디바이스 AI가 일상에 완벽하게 구현된 순간이었다.

24일(현지시간) 미국 하와이 마우이에서 열린 '스냅드래곤 서밋 2026' 데모 룸은 퀄컴의 차세대 칩셋을 품고 일상으로 다가온 스마트글래스의 현재와 미래를 볼 수 있는 공간이었다. 이곳에서 프리즘ML, 스펙스(SPECS), 엑스리얼(XREAL) 등 최신 증강현실(AR) 글래스 3종을 체험했다.

먼저 착용한 프리즘ML의 스마트글래스는 조작법이 매우 직관적이었다. 오른쪽 상단에 위치한 물리 버튼을 가볍게 누르면 사진이 찍히고, 이후 해당 피사체에 대해 질문을 던지면 AI가 음성으로 답을 해준다. 물병 외에도 현장에서 나눠준 트레이딩 카드를 향해 색깔을 묻자 지체 없이 "파란색"이라는 명확한 답변이 돌아왔다.

오프라인 온디바이스 AI 비결은 퀄컴 스냅드래곤 AR1 플랫폼과 프리즘ML의 압축 기술에 있다. 기존 8비트(bit)로 연산하던 무거운 AI 모델을 1비트 단위로 압축해 메모리 장벽을 깬 것이다.

지아드 아스가르 퀄컴 수석 부사장은 전날 기조연설에서 "1비트 모델 기술은 시각 장애인에게 주변 환경과 사물 정보를 실시간 전달해 줌으로써, 그들이 어려운 상황을 안전하게 헤쳐 나가도록 돕는 강력한 혁신이 될 것"이라고 강조하기도 했다.

두 번째로 체험한 스펙스(SPECS) AR 글래스는 마치 마법사가 된 듯한 몰입감을 선사했다. 이 제품의 가장 큰 특징은 별도의 물리적 컨트롤러 없이 오직 사용자 손바닥과 손가락 제스처만으로 모든 조작이 가능하다는 점이다.

빈 손바닥을 펼쳐 바라보면 허공에 메뉴 창이 떠오르고, 검지와 엄지로 살짝 꼬집는 모션을 취하자 원하는 앱이 선택됐다. 데모로 준비된 해리포터 게임을 실행하자 눈앞에 해리의 올빼미 '헤드위그'가 나타났다. 헤드위그를 향해 오라고 손짓한 뒤 오른팔을 길게 내밀자, 실제 팔 위에 올빼미가 사뿐히 내려앉았다. 물리적 현실과 디지털 그래픽이 정교하게 결합해 마치 영화 속으로 직접 들어가 주인공 해리포터가 된 듯한 짜릿한 기분을 느낄 수 있었다.

마지막으로 체험한 엑스리얼(XREAL)의 AR 글래스를 통해서는 '공간 컴퓨팅'을 체험할 수 있었다. 안경을 착용하자 텅 빈 현실의 공간 위에 거대한 가상 다중 모니터가 선명하게 펼쳐졌다. 여러 개의 웹 브라우저와 동영상 화면을 허공 원하는 위치에 고정(핀업)해두고 고개를 돌릴 때마다 자연스럽게 작업 화면을 오갈 수 있었다.

일반 뿔테 안경과 크게 다르지 않은 외관과 가벼운 착용감을 유지하면서도, 여러 개의 고해상도 화면을 띄운 채 머리를 빠르게 움직여도 화면 끊김이나 어지럼증이 전혀 느껴지지 않았다. 무거운 AR 연산과 공간 트래킹(추적)을 매끄럽게 소화하는 스냅드래곤 칩셋 최적화 성능이 돋보이는 대목이었다.

스냅드래곤의 무대는 이제 사용자 눈앞으로 옮겨왔다. AI와 공간 컴퓨팅을 가벼운 안경 하나에 압축한 3종의 스마트글래스는 스마트폰 이후 차세대 폼팩터 주도권 역시 퀄컴 스냅드래곤 생태계가 쥐고 있음을 증명했다.

items.content:
호주 주요 전력시장인 국가전력시장(NEM)에서 재생에너지가 전체 전력소비의 80% 이상을 공급하는 기록이 처음 나왔다. 옥상태양광 출력도 17GW에 근접하며 사상 최고 수준을 기록했다.

호주 전력시장 데이터 분석업체 글로벌파워에너지(Global Power Energy·GPE)가 호주에너지시장운영기관(AEMO) 자료를 분석한 결과 지난 19일(현지시간) 낮 12시30분께 NEM 전체 전력소비에서 재생에너지가 차지하는 비중은 80.5%까지 상승했다.

이는 불과 하루 전 기록한 79.84%를 넘어선 수준이다. 다만 80.5%는 하루나 분기 전체 평균이 아니라 전력시장이 5분 단위로 운영되는 과정에서 기록한 순간 최고치다.

기록 당시 NEM 전체 전력소비는 약 32.54GW였으며 옥상태양광 출력은 약 16.84GW에 달했다. 전체 전력소비의 약 52%에 해당하는 규모다. 가정과 상업시설 등에 설치된 분산형 태양광이 낮 시간대 전력공급의 핵심 발전원으로 자리 잡은 모습이다.

실제 옥상태양광 출력은 다음날인 20일(현지시간) 정오 1만6993MW까지 올라 다시 최고치를 경신했다. 전날 기록한 1만6837MW보다 156MW 높았으며 1년 전 같은 시기와 비교하면 약 13.4% 증가했다.

재생에너지 가용 출력이 늘면서 실제 발전으로 이어지지 못한 출력제한량도 크게 증가했다. 19일 재생에너지 비중이 80.5%에 도달한 시점에는 약 8.42GW의 태양광·풍력 발전 가능 출력이 제한됐다. 태양광 약 4.23GW, 풍력 약 4.19GW가 실제 발전으로 이어지지 못했다.

반면 배터리와 양수발전은 낮 시간대 남는 전력을 흡수하는 역할을 확대했다. 같은 시간 유연성 자원에 약 5.33GW의 전력이 투입됐으며 이 가운데 배터리 충전이 약 4.46GW, 양수발전이 약 880MW를 차지했다.

다음날에는 출력제한도 새로운 최고치를 기록했다. 20일 오전 11시55분께 NEM에서는 약 11.11GW의 태양광·풍력 발전 가능 출력이 제한됐다. 지난해 10월 기록한 종전 최고치 약 10.85GW를 웃돌았다.

옥상태양광 확대는 전력망에서 직접 공급해야 하는 전력수요도 낮추고 있다. 20일 NEM의 운영수요는 9422MW까지 떨어져 종전 최저치였던 지난해 10월4일의 9666MW를 244MW 밑돌았다.

운영수요는 소비자가 실제 사용하는 전체 전력에서 옥상태양광처럼 전력망 밖에서 자체 공급되는 전력을 제외하고 중앙 전력망이 공급해야 하는 수요를 의미한다. 따라서 옥상태양광이 늘어날수록 낮 시간대 운영수요가 크게 낮아질 수 있다.

NEM은 퀸즐랜드와 뉴사우스웨일스, 빅토리아, 사우스오스트레일리아, 태즈메이니아를 연결하는 호주 최대 전력시장이다. 서호주와 노던테리토리는 NEM에 포함되지 않는다.

재생에너지 비중 상승은 단기적인 순간 기록에 그치지 않고 중장기 전력구성 변화에서도 나타나고 있다. AEMO에 따르면 지난해 4분기에는 재생에너지와 저장장치가 NEM 전체 전력수요의 절반 이상을 처음으로 한 분기 동안 공급했다. 올해 1분기에도 재생에너지 발전비중은 46.5%로 역대 1분기 가운데 가장 높았다.

다만 재생에너지 출력 증가와 함께 대규모 출력제한도 동시에 확대되고 있다는 점은 과제로 남는다. 태양광과 풍력 발전량이 집중되는 시간대의 전력을 다른 시간대로 옮길 배터리와 양수발전, 송전망과 유연성 자원을 얼마나 빠르게 확충하느냐가 추가 보급량을 실제 전력공급으로 연결하는 핵심 변수가 될 전망이다.

items.content:
백악관 정상회담 돌입…AI 사고 통보·정보 공유·공통 안전기준 등 협력 방안 주목

컴퓨팅 입력 :2026/09/25 09:14 수정: 2026/09/25 10:09

미국과 중국 정상이 인공지능(AI) 개발·안전관리를 두고 시각차를 드러냈다. 미국은 AI가 가져올 평화와 번영을 부각한 반면, 중국은 AI가 인간 통제 아래 발전하도록 양국이 책임을 다해야 한다고 강조했다.

도널드 트럼프 미국 대통령과 시진핑 중국 국가주석은 24일(현지시간) 미국 워싱턴DC 백악관에서 정상회담에서 이같은 의견을 공유한 것으로 전해졌다. 회담은 소인수 회담과 확대 회담으로 나눠 비공개로 진행됐으며 모두발언은 공개되지 않았다.

트럼프 대통령은 회담에 앞선 환영식 연설에서 안보·기술과 함께 슈퍼지능(SI)을 주요 의제로 제시했다. 이 분야에서 내리는 결정이 앞으로 수십 년간 평화와 번영을 증진할 수 있다며 AI 발전의 긍정적 효과에 무게를 뒀다.

트럼프 대통령 발언은 AI 경쟁 우위를 유지하기 위해 개발을 이어가야 한다는 기존 미국 기조와 일맥상통한다. 그는 이날 오전 소셜미디어 트루스소셜에서도 AI 관련 입장을 이같이 유지하고 싶다는 뜻을 밝혔다. 지난 22일 유엔(UN)총회 연설에서는 AI에 대한 국제적 통제 구상에 반대했다.

시 주석은 같은 자리에서 AI 대국인 미중 양국이 기술 개발과 규제에 책임을 다해야 한다는 입장을 밝혔다. AI가 언제나 인간의 통제 아래 발전하고 사람들의 행복에 기여해야 한다는 점을 강조했다.

중국은 기술 혁신과 산업 활용을 확대하면서 위험관리도 병행해야 한다는 입장이다. 시 주석은 지난 7월 상하이 세계인공지능대회에서도 AI 산업 발전을 강조하는 동시에 위험 조기경보와 긴급대응 체계를 마련해야 한다고 밝혔다.

중국 당국은 지난 14일 AI 안전 거버넌스 프레임워크 3.0도 발표했다. AI 위험을 분류하고 기술적 대응과 관리 방안을 갱신해 안전성과 통제 가능성을 확보하기 위한 조치다.

美 업계·의회는 속도조절 촉구…中은 안전 명분 기술 견제 경계

그동안 미국 AI 업계에서는 안전 역량이 기술 발전을 따라갈 시간을 확보해야 한다는 목소리가 나왔다.

다리오 아모데이 앤트로픽 최고경영자(CEO)는 이달 공개한 기고문에서 AI가 다음 세대 AI 개발에 쓰이면서 기능 향상 속도가 인간 이해와 통제를 앞지를 수 있다고 경고했다.

아모데이 CEO는 외부 평가자의 기업 내 상주와 공통 안전기준 마련, 중국을 포함한 국제 협력을 제안했다. 모델 훈련을 이어가면서도 기업이 안전조치를 마련하고 제3자가 이를 검증할 시간을 확보하자는 취지다.

그는 미국과 동맹국이 AI 우위를 유지해야 한다며 중국에 대한 첨단 AI칩과 반도체 제조장비 수출통제도 주장했다. 안전을 위한 국제 공조를 추진하면서 기술 경쟁에서는 미국이 우위를 지켜야 한다는 입장이다.

미국 의회 일각에서는 더 강한 조치를 요구해 왔다. 크리스 밴홀런 의원 등 민주당 상원의원 17명은 지난 23일 트럼프 대통령에게 보낸 서한에서 시 주석과 첨단 AI 개발·시험·사용에 관한 안전장치와 국제 기준을 협의하라고 촉구했다. 사이버공격과 생물무기 개발 등 위험을 막기 위해 두 국가가 개발 속도를 늦추고 상호 일시정지까지 검토하는 공식 합의를 추진하라는 요구다.

중국은 AI 안전 논의가 자국을 겨냥한 기술 견제로 이어지는 데 반발하고 있다. 궈자쿤 중국 외교부 대변인은 아모데이 CEO 등의 주장에 대해 위협 담론과 대립이 글로벌 AI 거버넌스를 방해한다며 개방성과 포용성을 높여야 한다는 입장 밝혔다.

양국의 안전 협력이 구체화하려면 사고 통보 대상과 정보 공유 범위 등에 관한 접점을 찾을 필요가 있다는 제안이 나오고 있다. 크리스토퍼 콜린스 미국 전략국제문제연구소 연구원은 지난 21일 보고서에서 공통 정의와 사고 보고 채널, 기본적인 안전시험 절차 등 범위를 좁힌 의제에 집중할 것을 제안했다.

AI 안전 협의가 대중국 기술통제 완화로까지 이어질지는 불확실하다. 양국이 위험관리를 위한 협력 방안을 논의하더라도 첨단 기술의 수출 허용 여부는 별도 쟁점으로 남아 있다.

제이미슨 그리어 미국 무역대표부 대표는 지난 20일 진행된 AI 실무협의와 관련해 "첨단 AI칩과 반도체 제조장비의 수출통제 문제는 다뤄지지 않았다"며 "양국 실무대화가 곧바로 대중국 기술통제 완화로 이어진 것은 아닐 것"이라고 밝혔다.

items.content:
학생 발달 단계 따라 조절…판단·검증 능력 교육 강화

컴퓨팅 입력 :2026/09/25 09:09

생성형 인공지능(AI)이 숙제와 과제의 답까지 대신 내놓으면서 학교 교육이 AI를 '잘 쓰는 법'에서 '언제, 어떻게 쓰게 할 것인가'로 눈을 돌리고 있다.

25일 교육계에 따르면 국내외 교육 당국은 학생의 연령과 발달 단계에 따라 생성형 AI 활용 범위를 달리하거나 AI가 만든 정보를 비판적으로 판단하는 능력을 교육·평가하는 방안을 도입하고 있다. 서울시교육청은 최근 학생들의 AI 활용 능력과 함께 결과를 검증하는 역량까지 진단했고 미국 뉴욕시와 아랍에미리트(UAE) 아부다비 등은 연령별 AI 사용·교육 기준을 마련했다.

교육계에서는 학생이 AI에 답을 먼저 요구하는 일이 늘수록 스스로 생각하는 과정을 어떻게 유지할지가 중요하다는 지적이 나온다.

김봉제 서울교대 AI가치판단디자인센터장은 지디넷코리아와의 통화에서 "AI 네이티브 세대일수록 '사고 근육'을 기르는 과정이 중요하다"고 말했다.

학생이 직접 답을 찾기보다 AI가 만든 결과를 선택하고 활용하는 일이 늘어도 그 답이 맞는지 판단할 지식과 사고력이 저절로 생기는 것은 아니라는 설명이다. 김 센터장은 생각하는 과정을 반복해서 AI에 맡기면서 쌓이는 부담을 '인지적 부채'라고 표현했다.

그는 초등학교에서는 생성형 AI 사용을 상당 부분 제한하고 중학교 초반까지는 부모나 교사의 감독 아래 활용한 뒤 고등학교부터 범위를 넓히는 방안을 제시했다. AI 역시 정답부터 내놓기보다 질문과 힌트를 통해 학생이 한 번 더 생각하도록 설계할 필요가 있다고 설명했다.

국내 교육 현장에서도 AI를 얼마나 능숙하게 사용하는지만 보는 데서 벗어나 결과를 판단하고 검증하는 능력까지 살피려는 시도가 시작됐다.

서울시교육청은 이달 7일부터 18일까지 학생 대상 AI·디지털 리터러시 진단검사를 진행했다. 생성형 AI 활용 능력뿐 아니라 AI가 만든 정보를 비판적으로 판단하고 주체적·책임감 있게 사용하는 능력, 인간과 AI가 함께 문제를 해결하는 협업 역량까지 진단 대상에 포함했다.

진단 결과는 학생별 강점과 부족한 역량을 파악해 수업과 보완 교육에 활용한다. 가정에도 관련 학습자료를 제공해 학생의 AI 활용 방식을 함께 점검하도록 했다.

박형빈 서울교대 윤리교육과 교수는 "AI에 생각과 판단을 계속 맡기다 보면 '인지의 외주화'가 일어날 수 있다"며 "AI 리터러시는 단순히 AI를 잘 사용하는 능력이 아니라 AI가 내놓은 결과를 의심하고 스스로 검증할 수 있는 능력까지 포함해야 한다"고 말했다.

해외에서도 연령별 사용 제한과 교육과정 개편, 평가 방식 변경 등 서로 다른 방식으로 대응하고 있다.

뉴욕시는 2026~2027학년도부터 유아 과정인 2-K부터 8학년까지 학생의 생성형 AI 직접 사용을 금지했다. 고등학생은 학교가 승인한 프로그램만 사용할 수 있다. AI 작동 원리와 개인정보, 편향 등에 대한 교육도 함께 받는다.

아랍에미리트(UAE) 아부다비는 170개 이상 사립학교에서 연령별 AI 리터러시 교육을 운영한다. 유아 단계에서는 AI 도구를 직접 사용하기보다 화면을 쓰지 않는 활동으로 논리적·비판적 사고를 기르고 학년이 올라갈수록 AI 결과 평가와 문제 해결 등으로 활용 범위를 넓힌다.

호주 뉴사우스웨일스주는 생성형 AI 확산에 맞춰 고교 평가 방식을 바꿨다. 올해 4학기부터 집에서 작성하는 고교 졸업시험(HSC) 평가 과제를 과목당 한 개, 학교 평가 점수의 최대 15%로 제한한다.

김 센터장은 "AI 사용을 '금지냐 허용이냐'로만 나눠서는 안 된다"며 "사고의 근육이 형성되기 전까지는 어느 정도 거리를 둬야 편향된 정보가 제공됐을 때도 생각하는 힘으로 다시 검증할 수 있다"고 말했다.

items.content:
양사 3분기 영업이익률, 전년비 2%p 감소 전망

반도체ㆍ디스플레이 입력 :2026/09/25 09:08

삼성디스플레이와 LG디스플레이의 3분기 영업이익률이 전년비 소폭 감소할 것으로 관측된다. 주요 고객 유기발광다이오드(OLED) 출하량은 견조하지만, 환율 급락과 메모리 반도체 가격 상승 여파가 크다.

삼성디스플레이와 LG디스플레이의 영업손익은 주요 고객인 애플의 아이폰 신제품 출시 일정에 따라 '상저하고' 실적 흐름을 보여 왔다. 업계에서는 두 기업의 3분기 수익성이 당초 기대보다 부진할 것이라는 우려가 나온다. 불리한 환율과 IT 시장 위축, 설비투자에 따른 감가상각 등이 부담이다.

25일 증권가에 따르면 삼성디스플레이의 3분기 영업이익은 약 1조 1000억원으로 예상된다. 비수기였던 전 분기 대비로는 54.9% 높지만, 전년 동기 대비로는 9.6% 낮 다. 영업이익률 예상치는 13%로, 전년 동기(15%) 대비 2%p 낮다.

백길현 유안타증권 연구원은 최근 보고서에서 "3분기는 주력 고객 폴더블폰 판매 호조에도 불구하고, 8.6세대 IT OLED 양산 개시에 따른 감가상각비와 북미 고객 중심의 판가 인하 압박 영향이 있었다"며 "전년 동기 대비 수익성은 약 2%p 훼손이 불가피할 전망"이라고 설명했다.

LG디스플레이 역시 3분기 기대에 못 미치는 성적을 거둘 것으로 예상된다.

키움증권은 최근 보고서에서 LG디스플레이가 3분기 매출 6조 6745억원, 영업이익 2572억원을 거둘 것으로 내다봤다. 각각 전년 동기 대비 4%, 40% 감소한 수준이다. 영업이익 전망치는 증권가 컨센서스 4291억원을 크게 밑돈다. 해당 분기 영업이익률 전망치는 4% 수준이다. 전년 동기(6%) 대비 2%p 적다.

권민규 키움증권 연구원은 "환율 급락과 칩플레이션, 세트 가격 상승으로 IT 수요 감소가 예상된다"며 "다만 하반기 모바일 OLED 출하량은 전년 대비 15% 증가하는 등 안정적인 출하는 지속될 것"이라고 설명했다.

원·달러 환율은 6월 말 1537원 수준에서 9월 23일 기준 1362원 수준으로 10% 이상 하락했다. 디스플레이를 포함한 부품 업계는 메모리 반도체 가격 급등으로 고객사로부터 받는 단가 인하 압박이 커졌다.

한편, 지난 23일 LG디스플레이는 탑런토탈솔루션과 지난 2월 체결했던 1040억원 규모 중국 난징 차량 액정표시장치(LCD) 모듈 사업 양수도 계약을 해지했다고 밝혔다. 당초 양수도 예정일도 7월 말이었지만, 9월 말로 연기된 바 있다.

LG디스플레이는 23일 공시에서 "(지난 2월) 사업구조 고도화와 수익구조 강화를 위해 차량 LCD 모듈 사업 부문을 양도 후 외주화하기로 결정했다"면서도 "양사가 주요 조건 세부사항을 계속 협의했지만 거래 완결과 관련한 최종 합의에 이르지 못해 영업양도 결정을 철회했다"고 설명했다.

items.content:
영국이 전력망 접속을 기다리는 배터리에 추가 재정 보증을 요구하는 방안을 추진한다. 실제 건설 가능성이 낮은 사업이 접속 용량을 선점하는 것을 막기 위해 프로젝트 규모에 따라 메가와트(MW)당 최대 2만5000파운드(약 4500만원)를 담보하도록 하는 방식이다.

영국 에너지 규제기관 오프젬(Ofgem)은 지난 17일(현지시간) 배터리에 ‘과잉신청 기술 약정 부담금(OTCF)’을 도입하는 계통이용규정 개정안 CMP470을 승인하는 방향으로 검토하고 있다고 밝혔다. 현재 업계 의견수렴이 진행 중이며 최종 결정은 올해 안에 내려질 예정이다.

이번 제도는 그레이트브리튼 지역의 전력망 접속 대기열에 포함된 배터리에 우선 적용될 가능성이 크다. 현재 약 7기가와트(GW)의 배터리가 가동 중이고, 국가에너지시스템운영기관(NESO)이 개편한 접속 대기열에는 추가로 83GW가 우선순위 프로젝트로 남아 있다.

가동 설비와 접속 대기 프로젝트를 합하면 약 90GW로, 2035년 영국 전력시스템에 필요할 것으로 예상되는 배터리 규모 약 29GW의 3배를 웃돈다. NESO는 앞선 계통접속 개편 과정에서 기준을 충족하지 못한 전력망급 배터리 프로젝트 용량의 약 40%를 대기열에서 제외했지만 여전히 과잉 신청이 이어지고 있다.

오프젬은 이처럼 실제 필요한 용량보다 많은 프로젝트가 대기열에 남아 있을 경우 어떤 사업이 실제로 건설될지 파악하기 어려워지고, 전력망 운영·투자계획에도 불확실성이 커진다고 판단했다. 건설 가능성이 낮은 사업이 계통 접속 위치를 장기간 차지할 경우 실제 추진 가능한 사업의 접속도 늦어질 수 있다는 설명이다.

제안된 제도에서는 과잉신청 상태가 일정 수준을 넘으면 사업자가 용량에 비례한 재정 보증을 제공해야 한다. 초기 기준은 MW당 3000파운드(약 540만원)이며 과잉 상태가 지속될 경우 최대 MW당 2만5000파운드(약 4500만원)까지 높아진다.

예를 들어 100MW 규모 배터리 사업에 최고 수준의 보증이 적용되면 필요한 금액은 250만파운드(약 45억원)에 이른다. 다만 기존 계통접속 절차에서 이미 제공한 보증액이 새 기준보다 많다면 CMP470 때문에 추가 담보를 별도로 제공할 필요는 없다.

원안에서는 특정 기술의 접속 대기용량이 정부가 정한 목표 필요량을 50% 넘게 초과할 경우 제도를 가동하고, 초과 규모가 25% 미만으로 내려가면 적용을 중단하도록 설계됐다. NESO가 과잉신청 수준을 확인하고 보증 수준을 결정·관리하게 된다.

재정 보증은 단순히 납부한 뒤 돌려받지 못하는 일회성 수수료와는 차이가 있다. 사업자가 프로젝트를 계속 추진하면 필요한 재정 보증을 유지하고, 실제 계통에 연결돼 가동되면 OTCF는 사업자에게 반환된다. 반대로 발전·저장설비가 실제로 가동되지 않은 상태에서 대기열을 이탈하고 OTCF가 계약 해지 비용에 포함돼 징수되면 해당 금액은 송전망 이용요금을 통해 소비자에게 돌려주는 구조다.

CMP470은 배터리 개발사 필드에너지(Field Energy)가 올해 3월 제안한 계통접속 및 시스템이용규정 개정안이다. 오프젬이 승인하면 NESO가 제도를 운영하며, 현재 일정상 실제 재정 보증 적용은 2027년 하반기부터 시작될 가능성이 있다.

오프젬은 배터리 자체의 보급을 억제하는 것이 제도의 목적은 아니라는 입장이다. 재생에너지 발전량 변동에 대응하려면 대규모 배터리 확대가 필요하지만, 실제 추진 가능성이 낮은 사업까지 계통 접속 용량을 확보한 상태로 장기간 남아 있는 문제를 줄여야 한다는 것이다.

오프젬은 다음달 1일(현지시간)까지 이번 방안에 대한 의견을 받고 올해 안에 최종 결정을 내릴 예정이다. 현재 원안 외에도 보증액과 적용기간, 공동입지 사업의 처리 방식 등을 달리한 6개 대안이 함께 검토되고 있어 실제 적용기준은 최종 결정 과정에서 달라질 수 있다.

items.title: Meta employees ordered ‘attorney/client privilege’ hats while fighting child safety disclosures
items.summary: Meta's lawyers have argued that certain evidence should be withheld from public view on the grounds of attorney-client privilege in the ongoing lawsuits over alleged harm to teens' safety and mental health. Lawyers suing the company said this week that the label has been applied
items.content:
Lawyers suing Meta called the hats an example of its ‘culture of privilege abuse.’

Meta’s lawyers have argued that certain evidence should be withheld from public view on the grounds of attorney-client privilege in the ongoing lawsuits over alleged harm to teens’ safety and mental health . Lawyers suing the company said this week that the label has been applied far too broadly, while pointing to a recently unsealed document showing that the team behind launching Instagram’s Teen Accounts in 2024 put in an order for baseball caps that simply said “a/c priv.”

The lawyers suing Meta argue the Project Nido (an internal name for the Teen Accounts team) swag is part of “culture of privilege abuse at Meta” aimed at keeping the research it’s conducted internally on teen harm out of the public eye, an issue that Mark Zuckerberg discussed after internal data on Instagram’s effects leaked in 2021.

US District Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers already called some of Meta’s privilege redactions “entirely inappropriate” in an order last month .

She pointed out one example where Meta’s lawyers tried to cast a discussion about a slide deck and whether or not to publish certain data as a discussion of attorney legal advice, deciding that based on testimony from the trial, their reticence about publishing was more of a business decision focused on preventing leaks.

Meta de-designated about 65,000 previously withheld or redacted documents in April 2025, after discovery, which the plaintiffs say came too late for them to use in depositions. Now Meta has requested time through the end of this year to re-review other privilege redactions it’s made, while the plaintiffs’ lawyers say a neutral party should be appointed to lead the review, paid for by Meta.

items.title: Qualcomm’s new ‘Elite’ sound chip might finally deliver the Wi-Fi earbud dream
items.summary: What if your wireless earbuds - or audio glasses - could stream high-quality lossless audio that doesn't cut out when you leave your phone on the bedside charger or buried in the couch? Qualcomm's new Snapdragon Sound Elite Gen 2 is its first to integrate "micro-power Wi-Fi 6E" r
items.content:
Also, they do AI for “intelligent hearables.”

What if your wireless earbuds — or audio glasses — could stream high-quality lossless audio that doesn’t cut out when you leave your phone on the bedside charger or buried in the couch? Qualcomm’s new Snapdragon Sound Elite Gen 2 is its first to integrate “micro-power Wi-Fi 6E” right into the chip, so they can connect directly to your home Wi-Fi network, and from there to the cloud.

If that sounds like a familiar promise, it’s probably because Qualcomm promised something similar back in 2023 with the “S7 Pro sound platform” and its Expanded Personal Area Network (XPAN) tech, saying that Wi-Fi earbuds can do what Bluetooth alone cannot. Namely, 24-bit 96kHz lossless audio that can’t fit into Bluetooth’s meager bandwidth.

But that old 7-series platform required a separate Wi-Fi chip to give you Wi-Fi earbuds, and it seems that wasn’t a winning formula for getting makers of incredibly tiny devices to adopt the tech! In fact, we’ve only ever heard of one: Xiaomi’s 2025 Buds 5 Pro , which didn’t get a global release.

Now that Wi-Fi no longer requires an extra chip, perhaps the idea can take off. Qualcomm says the Elite is also 30 percent smaller, consumes up to 40 percent less power, and has twice the AI processing capabilities of the previous gen chip, all of which should be music to device makers’ ears.

So far, Qualcomm says it’s working with HP on one specific unnamed product, is “working closely with Bose,” and is “pioneering a new category of intelligent hearables” (read: earbuds with built-in cameras) with Cleer.

월스트리트저널(WSJ)은 24일(현지시간) 비영리 AI 연구소 트랜슬루스(Transluce)의 연구 결과를 인용해 오픈AI 연관 AI 에이전트들이 5월과 6월 주요 기관 웹사이트에 무단 침입해 정보를 추출하려 했다고 보도했다. 여기에는 호주 보건복지연구소, 뉴멕시코대학교, 공공 데이터 프로젝트인 데이터 USA 등이 포함됐다.

이번 해킹 시도는 모델의 사이버 보안 평가용 테스트가 아니라 인터넷 공개 정보 검색 능력을 훈련하고 벤치마킹하는 내부 테스트 과정에서 발생한 것으로 알려졌다. 수집 대상 정보는 태국의 노동 통계, 한국의 원유 수입량, 호주의 피부과 데이터 등 기본적인 온라인 데이터였으나, 웹사이트 접속 제한이나 블록을 맞닥뜨리자 악성 페이로드를 질의에 첨부하는 등 해킹 기술을 동원해 우회를 시도했다.

이번 사고도 앞서 허깅페이스 등에서 포착된 데이터 수집용 AI 에이전트와 동일한 시스템에 의해 발생한 것으로 분석됐다.

앞서 호주 정부는 오픈AI 에이전트가 공공 데이터를 제공하는 정부 웹사이트 4곳에서 데이터 수집을 시도했으며, 이 중 호주 정부 보건보험 프로그램의 공공 통계 포털 백엔드 인프라에 무단 접근했다고 밝혔다. 앤서니 앨버니지 호주 총리는 AI 에이전트가 공공 보건 통계 포털 내 비공개 파일까지 접근 권한을 획득했음을 확인했다.

트랜슬루스 연구진에 따르면 이번 공격으로 비공개 정보가 실제 유출되거나 다운로드됐다는 증거는 확인되지 않았다. 연구진은 에이전트들이 자동 접근 방지 조치를 우회하기 위해 온라인 브라우징 도구를 활용하는 과정에서 악의적인 방식으로 정렬이 이탈했다고 분석했다.

오픈AI 대변인은 이번 사건을 '오정렬 활동(misaligned activity)'으로 규정하고 광범위한 검토를 진행 중이라고 밝혔다. 또 영향받은 기관들에 관련 사실을 알렸으며, 웹사이트 스팸 전송과 같은 저위험 사건을 포함한 전체적인 조사는 완료까지 수개월이 걸릴 것이라고 덧붙였다.

items.title: Microsoft puts Brad Smith in charge of communications
items.summary: Microsoft is moving its communications group out of marketing and into its Corporate, External, and Legal Affairs (CELA) organization. The surprise change will see Microsoft vice chair and president Brad Smith oversee communications, while the company searches for a replacement f
items.content:
Microsoft’s communications are moving over to the legal and corporate side of the house.

Microsoft is moving its communications group out of marketing and into its Corporate, External, and Legal Affairs (CELA) organization. The surprise change will see Microsoft vice chair and president Brad Smith oversee communications, while the company searches for a replacement for Frank Shaw, chief communications officer, who is departing later this year.

Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella thanked Shaw “for everything he has done for Microsoft” in an internal memo announcing the communications changes. Shaw announced earlier this month that he’s leaving Microsoft after nearly three decades supporting the company’s communications.

Brent Colburn, VP of global public affairs, has been appointed as interim communications leader to help navigate what Nadella calls “a media environment that is increasingly fragmented and noisier than ever.” Nadella also says he’s “excited about the opportunity to help our engineers, sellers, partners, and others closest to our products and customers become an even bigger part of how we tell our story.”

As GeekWire points out , that sounds a lot like how AI startups work, with researchers leading the demos and blogs at companies like OpenAI and Anthropic. Microsoft has been chasing Google, Anthropic, and OpenAI to “become one of the top four labs in the world,” according to Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman. In an interview with The Verge earlier this year, Suleyman said he wants Microsoft “to build the very best frontier models in the world.”

Brad Smith, who’s taking over communications from chief marketing officer Takeshi Numoto, is often the public face of Microsoft’s policy and corporate communications. Smith travels the world meeting with governments, regulators, and Microsoft’s customers. It’s still not clear who will take over permanently from Shaw later this year, but Microsoft is looking at both internal and external candidates.

Here’s Satya Nadella’s memo:

Communications has never been more important to Microsoft. The company is changing, our industry is changing, and the world around us is changing. And in a media environment that is increasingly fragmented and noisier than ever, we need to continue to be grounded in our mission, earn trust each day, and find new ways to connect directly with all of our constituencies.

I first want to thank Frank for everything he has done for Microsoft. He has made tremendous contributions to the company and to our communications function over the last 17+ years. And he’s been a great source of counsel to our leadership team and to me personally, across the company’s biggest moments.

As Frank prepares to embark on his next chapter, Takeshi, Brad, and I have been discussing the evolution of comms at the company. I have asked Brad to lead the communications function going forward. Few leaders embody Microsoft’s voice as authentically as Brad. He brings a deep understanding of our business, a strong connection to our stakeholders, and a rare ability to communicate complex ideas with clarity, conviction, and trust.

During this transition, Brent Colburn will continue reporting to Brad and will now act as our interim communications leader. The comms leadership team will report to Brent, and Frank will continue to advise Brad and Brent on the transition.

In many ways, the people closest to the work have the best opportunity to shape how Microsoft is understood. We need to give people across the company the tools and support to do it well. And I’m excited about the opportunity to help our engineers, sellers, partners, and others closest to our products and customers become an even bigger part of how we tell our story, all connected by a shared strategy and set of principles. All of you have a critical role to play in making that possible.

We have an exciting fall ahead, with a number of important moments and events coming up and great marketing behind them. It is a real opportunity to bring together our product story, our marketing, and our communications in new ways.

We will learn, we will experiment, and we will evolve. There is a fundamentally new way to think about communications, and this team will be central to building it.

Thank you for everything you do for Microsoft, and for the role you each play in telling our story.

items.title: Nexterity wants to automate the hard, dangerous part of pipefitting
items.summary: The startup's robot can tighten or loosen four bolts at a time, and it fits in a Pelican case.
items.content:
Lindsey Elliott is big into bolts. At last year’s Bolting Symposium — the 13th annual — she said the highlight was playing “Bolting Bingo” against the many self-proclaimed “torque dorks” who were in the room.

A former engineer and planner at ExxonMobil, Elliott has spent years thinking about how to improve the infrastructure that moves oil, gas, and petrochemicals. Bolts are what she landed on. Specifically, the bolts that connect sections of pipe (technically called “bolted flange joints”). These bolts require hard, physical work to loosen and tighten, and are the source of many pipefitters’ injuries. Like many trade industries, there’s also a labor shortage.

“Those people get really tired when they’re asked to work 12 hours a day for three months in a row,” she told TechCrunch. “I’ve talked to pipefitters across the U.S. across Canada, and just repeatedly have been told North American pipefitting productivity is notoriously low.”

The solution Elliott came up with at her startup Nexterity, which is one of the Startup Battlefield 200 selected to participate in TechCrunch Disrupt, is a remote-controlled robot that can handle this part of the job. It’s the kind of idea that could fundamentally change this particular blue collar job if widely adopted, making the workers safer and more productive.

Think: more dork, less torque.

Elliott said Nexterity has developed a few different configurations of the robot to fit different standard pipe sizes, but they’re all small enough to fit in a Pelican case and be carried by a single worker. That makes them easy to deploy to new sites — flexibility that is crucial to Nexterity’s business model of treating the robot like rental construction equipment.

Elliott said she arrived at this particular design as a result of conversations she’s had over the last few years — not just at the Bolting Symposium, but also with members of the Pressure Vessels & Piping Division of the American Society of Mechanical Engineers.

“What I learned from the people, the torque dorks per se,” she said, “is that 80% of our pipes are between two to eight inches in diameter, or what they call NPS2 to NPS8. And so when you have that much repeatability, you have a fantastic candidate for automation.”

It’s a pretty straightforward idea, but one that Elliott believes has a lot of upside.

“I think it would shock a lot of people just how big this market is,” she said. “I mean, day to day, most of us don’t think about piping infrastructure, but even water, wastewater, water treatment, food and beverage, mining, nuclear, any kind of green and sustainable manufacturing facility — they all use the same kind of piping.”

items.title: When chat is the wrong UI
items.summary: What is a developer to do when they need something more tangible than a chat box? Enter canvases. The post When chat is the wrong UI appeared first on The GitHub Blog .
items.content:
We’re 176 years into this AI experiment.

Wait…it’s only been three years?

Sometimes I remember things that happened last year, but it feels like it was so long ago. Did that really happen to me, or was it something that happened to my dad and he just told me about it when I was a kid?

Anyway… we’re three years into this AI experiment and the primary interaction surface we have with LLMs is still chat. I’m pretty sure it was @pmarca who first argued for a textarea component in the HTML spec. And I’m pretty sure of that fact because I asked AI about it. In a textarea.

But I would like to propose to you that perhaps, just maybe, chat is the wrong UI. Well, at least most of the time.

The Academic Steven Pinker said it this way…

It’s kind of a shame that the first large-scale implementation of AI was kind of a gimmick—a first-person chatbot. But there is tremendous promise for AI if it is task oriented.

And if an academic says it and then I write it down as a quote in a blog post, then you know it’s true.

Chat is the primary way of working with AI because it was the first thing that people clicked with. And chat works really well as a universal solution simply because we don’t know what people are going to try to do with AI.

But as the user you know what you’re going to do with it, and at that point chat is often the wrong UI.

What you need, dear reader, is some sort of customizable UI that you can manifest out of thin air to work with the AI (or fight with—you do you) in the way that works for what you are trying to do in the moment.

There are lots of ways to pull this off, but in the GitHub Copilot app , this is called a canvas.

A canvas is a little full-stack application that runs inside of the GitHub Copilot app with no browser chrome. The agent can communicate with the server part of that app and the server can communicate back. So what you end up with is a surface that can do anything a normal computer program can do, plus can communicate bi-directionally with the GitHub Copilot agent.

That sounds very hand-wavy and I did use the word bi-directional which sounds like it’s straight off of a PowerPoint, so let’s look at this concept in practice and see if we can solve actual problems with the mighty canvas.

We’ll start with a simple example: using a canvas to create a Connect 4 game where you can play with the agent inside of the GitHub Copilot app.

Watch me absolutely DESTROY GPT-5.6 Sol on high reasoning…

OK. But I definitely did beat GPT-5.6 Luna with no reasoning so…LISTEN…CONNECT 4 IS A HARD GAME!!

Building a canvas is as simple as asking for it…

The GitHub Copilot app knows what a canvas is, so we don’t need to explain ourselves any more than that.

Now because these canvases are actually full stack apps and not just web pages, they can call third-party APIs, yes, but they can also execute code locally on your machine.

For example, here is a UI for Winget that can browse for packages on the registry, as well as manage my local packages, including installing and uninstalling.

There’s no AI here, but that’s the point.

When chat is the primary interface, it encourages you to use the agent to do everything. This is often just a pure waste of tokens. It’s almost always better to have the agent build a tool where all future interactions are free vs treating the agent itself as the tool. Stop asking GPT-5.6 Sol Max to “stage and commit”. (I know you do that. Because I’ve done it. Don’t token shame me, I have a fragile ego.)

Another great example would be instead of using the chat to ask the agent to do things with your SQLite database, how about you throw up a canvas and, you know, do it yourself.

I mean, you can even have intellisense here. Why not? Its 2026, and AI is a magical box that just does whatever you want.

Isn’t that pleasant?

It’s nice to write a little SQL every now and again. I said every now and again . Relax.

Or why write your Jekyll blog posts in plain Markdown when you can literally bring Windows Live Writer back from the dead.

Ok, these are all fun and mildly useful examples, but the value of custom UI gets a lot more clear when you use it to automate your development workflows.

I’m not going to tell you how to live your life, but my process for working with agents looks more or less like this…

It’s pretty simple, but each one of these steps requires me to be at the keyboard to interact, view prototypes, guide and move between steps.

But here’s the thing. I don’t actually need to be around for most of this process. The agent is capable of researching and generating prototypes and then letting me know when it’s ready for a review. The goal with agents is always to take yourself out of the loop as much as you can. That’s difficult though, because it’s not clear how to do that when all you have is a chat box.

Here’s a full example of how you can use a canvas to automate your own workflow, removing yourself from the loop as much or as little as you like.

I’m not saying you should copy this workflow or that this is the perfect example of how to work with agents. I mean, it might be. It probably is. Let’s ask AI…

In all seriousness, I do think being boxed in by the chat UI may be working against us all right now. This is making it hard to figure out how to solve actual problems, because it’s not at all obvious what to do when your only method of interaction is a textarea.

Give canvases a try today. Some things like the SQLite canvas you can one shot. The workflow one took the better part of a day to get the design and automation right.

But I think you’ll find that you can go much further with AI when you think…wait for it…outside the chat box.

items.title: Gemini 3.8 Live with Live Avatar gives Google’s AI a face
items.summary: Google's new Gemini 3.8 Live update lets users have conversations with the model while watching an animated AI persona respond in real time. The "Live Avatar" will lip-sync and show different facial expressions during conversations, but it's currently only available to Gemini Ent
items.content:
Google’s Live Avatar can lip-sync and show different facial expressions.

Google’s new Gemini 3.8 Live update lets users have conversations with the model while watching an animated AI persona respond in real time. The “Live Avatar” will lip-sync and show different facial expressions during conversations, but it’s currently only available to Gemini Enterprise customers.

As noted by Google, Live Avatar can transition between the 97 languages it supports “without degrading video fidelity or introducing visual drift.” One video shared by Google shows its Live Avatar talking in English and Japanese, with its mouth animation lining up with what it’s saying in both languages. It can also pull up information on-screen while it talks.

The launch of Live Avatar comes about a week after Google revealed its new Gemini 3.8 Live model , which the company says “processes visual inputs in near real-time.” Though Google will offer a library of preset avatars for customers to choose from, it will also allow organizations to create their own. Google says output from its Live Avatar comes with its invisible SynthID watermark alongside safeguards to “respect identity.”

items.title: I Think I Found an AI Agent Worth the Risk
items.summary: Instinct saved me $550, booked my restaurant reservations, and warned me about a phishing scam. It also wasted $64 and might be a security nightmare.
items.content:
One of the first things I did when I left my full-time job at WIRED was give Claude Cowork access to my email and calendar. After reporting on artificial intelligence for years, I was curious about what the technology could do for me. I had imagined Cowork as a hyper-capable digital assistant, but was let down to discover that it was more like interacting with a regular chatbot, albeit one with extra tools . What did I want it to do? I had no idea.

Then Instinct, an invite-only AI agent that communicates with users through iMessage and WhatsApp, started popping off in the Bay Area. It connects to your email, calendar, and messaging apps. Think of it as OpenClaw for normies. The company, which launched in private beta in February, is reportedly in talks to raise $1 billion on top of the $350 million it’s already raised, bringing its valuation to $10 billion, according to The Information.

The divide between people who use AI agents for everything and those who have never tried one has never been wider. It explains, in part, why tech CEOs were largely caught off guard by the data center backlash . If you think agents can automate the majority of people’s administrative drudgery and turbocharge their productivity, the costs and disruptions associated with building data centers might look like an acceptable trade-off. But if you’re using chatbots as a fancy form of Google, that deal is probably much less appealing.

The overarching problem, as technology journalist Jasmine Sun writes, is that “most people’s problems are not software-shaped, and most won’t notice even when they are.” AI agents, like chatbots, still require a lot of input and direction from users. If you know what you want— help with your homework , a virtual girlfriend —the tools are eager to provide. But if you don’t, well, welcome to the permanent underclass .

I was eager to avoid such a fate. I may not be agentic , but I like to think I’m action-oriented. Surely I could identify a software-shaped problem in my life. I had used Claude previously to generate a few freelance invoices, saving me approximately 10 minutes. It was nice, but not life-changing. I decided to give Instinct a try.

If you talk to AI researchers about Instinct, you’ll hear the phrase “form factor” a lot. Instinct got the form factor right—no open text box, just iMessage, WhatsApp, and a few helpful prompts. It’s hard to overstate how important this is. Rather than trying to figure out for yourself how to make the chat experience more useful, you’re texting with an agent that’s suggesting things it can do for you, and then actually doing them. And unlike other agents in this space, it doesn’t text too much. I tried a competing agent called Lindy for a week and deleted it after it texted me each morning and started popping into Zoom meetings without my approval.

For its first project, I gave Instinct my itinerary for a work trip to Venice, Italy. I had it book reservations based on where I was going to be, including WhatsApping hole-in-the-wall spots. Success! Restaurant reservations appear to be a gateway drug for many agent-curious people, and I was no exception. (It’s worth noting that while Muse can also call restaurants to book reservations on your behalf, some of those calls are reportedly made by humans in call centers, according to reporting in 404 Media ).

Next, I gave Instinct a more complicated task. I had already booked a trip to New York in November with my sister when WIRED asked me to attend the WIRED World Fair , which was taking place in Miami the day before. Unfortunately, I’d booked a saver fare, meaning I couldn’t move the ticket, and if I missed the first leg of the trip it would automatically cancel the whole thing.

Could Instinct cancel my trip and get a refund? To my surprise, it could. The agent detected that Alaska had moved my flight 90 minutes earlier, a fact I’d completely missed, which qualified me for a full refund. It canceled my ticket, saving me roughly $550, and rebooked my one-way return to San Francisco. I don’t know about you guys, but I’m starting to feel the AGI .

This is where I have to pause and acknowledge the risks of using Instinct. There are a lot. People have reported that when they tried to disconnect the agent from their email, they found out it was retaining a copy of their inboxes anyway. One venture capitalist said he was banned from Resy after the bot pinged its API roughly 200 times per hour while trying to make a reservation. Another tech investor said he deleted the app after determining that it would be trivially easy for Instinct to be phished.

Instinct’s Terms of Service are pretty far-reaching, allowing the company to use at least some of your conversations to train its AI models. I also experienced an annoying (if minor) snafu: One day, Instinct canceled a DoorDash order that was seriously delayed, forcing me to forfeit $64. (I’d explicitly told it to cancel only if I could get a refund.) This alerted me to another thing Instinct is very, very good at: profusely apologizing without offering to pay for its mistakes.

The company Instinct, which shares the same name as its flagship AI agent, did not respond to requests for comment from WIRED.

Instinct feels like a mildly chaotic personal assistant, and since I’ve never had a real human assistant, I’m sticking with it. Last week it told me “NOT TO OPEN” an email from a friend inviting me to a backyard BBQ—it turned out to be a phishing scam. Agents are a security nightmare. I get it! But I’m busy. I’m a mom. Everything feels like a security nightmare these days. For now, I’m willing to take the risk.

items.title: F-Droid gets its biggest update in a decade with new UI and smoother app installs
items.summary: F-Droid's Android app store has been rebuilt from the ground up.
items.content:
Virtually every Android device comes with the Play Store preloaded, but there are other ways to get apps. F-Droid bills itself as a community-driven source for free and open source Android apps, but its official app store has gone 10 years without a major update. That’s finally changing: After a multiyear effort, the team has just announced F-Droid 2.0 is rolling out.

The new F-Droid client was redesigned from scratch in Kotlin Compose, which is the standard for modern Android apps. This makes the store much more responsive, and there’s optional support for Android’s Material theming. The interface has also been cleaned up considerably, making the most important functions easier to access and hiding some others in overflow menus.

While the new F-Droid looks nicer, the update was largely about making it easier to find and install apps. When F-Droid first appeared, there wasn’t much to see, but now it has thousands of open source apps. Unlike the Play Store, F-Droid doesn’t track your taps and installs to push ads and suggestions—it helps you find things and gets out of the way.

F-Droid now includes a huge number of categories, drilling down to specialized niches like firewalls, password managers, and VPNs. You can see all these groups in the search tab. There are also higher-level categories listed on the main Discover page. When searching for apps, F-Droid will now be able to return results based on app descriptions rather than just names.

When you find an app, F-Droid 2.0 will make the installation process easier. Google has long put up roadblocks for sideloaded apps, citing the security implications. This is also the rationale behind its upcoming developer verification system . For now at least, apps will be easier to install from F-Droid thanks to the use of Google’s pre-approval API. Instead of downloading an APK, opening it, and confirming the scary sideloading pop-up, you’ll just be able to verify that you want to install an app before the download. So you tap “Install” in F-Droid, and then tap “Install” again in a system pop-up. That’s one more click than the Play Store, but it’s still an improvement.

The team also says that F-Droid 2.0 will automatically check for and install app updates (unless you disable this). It can also download and install multiple apps simultaneously. Given the auto-updates, F-Droid no longer uses pull-to-refresh on the app screen, which the developers acknowledge may upset their particular user base. Manual updates are still available in the three-dot menu for peace of mind.

Here’s the highlighted changelog from F-Droid.

New in version 2.0.0

The new F-Droid client is rolling out in stages over the next two weeks—the default installer on the F-Droid site hasn’t been replaced yet. If you want the 2.0 release right now, it’s available on the versions page . The official client is not the only way to access F-Droid apps, but now you’ll have less reason to seek out an alternative.

items.title: PrismML brings its tiny LLMs to Qualcomm-powered smart glasses
items.summary: Prism's larger goal is open-weight AI that runs on devices and makes better use of the computing power they already have.
items.content:
The AI Lab PrismML — founded by Caltech researchers and advised by UC Berkeley’s Ion Stoica — has created a version of its tiny language models for smart glasses running on Qualcomm’s Snapdragon chips.

On Wednesday, at Qualcomm’s Snapdragon Summit, the chipmaker showcased PrismML’s 1-bit Bonsai LLM, which can be run locally on AI smart glasses built on the Snapdragon AR1 Gen 1 Platform.

As TechCrunch previously reported, PrismML’s claim to fame is that it shrinks larger models substantially (in this case, by 4x), while retaining almost all of their performance on standard benchmarks. The smart glasses version is a 2-billion-parameter model tuned for vision and language, so wearers can ask what they’re looking at in real time.

Prism’s larger goal is open-weight AI that runs on devices and makes better use of the computing power they already have. The startup pitches this as an alternative to depending on the privacy promises of proprietary AI labs and their insatiable need for more compute.

Releasing a model for Qualcomm’s chip is a step toward that vision. But no smart glasses running PrismML have been announced yet.

items.title: Meet Feather, the startup building the ‘Android of robotics’ for developers
items.summary: Feather is betting on a customizable, $30,000 platform built for software developers.
items.content:
If there is one thing robotics founders and investors agree on, it’s that the “ChatGPT moment” where a general-purpose robot can seamlessly adapt to any environment has not arrived. Opinions vary on whether the breakthrough is just around the corner or a decade away.

Feather Robotics , a humanoid startup founded last year, is developing a robot for either timeline. Unlike Tesla or Figure, which are tackling the lofty mission of building both the body and a foundational “brain” that isn’t yet widely deployed, Feather provides the hardware and software toolkit for developers to tackle real-world tasks now.

“You can’t buy a Tesla robot today and develop on top of it,” Feather co-founder Hoa Mai told TechCrunch. “We realized that this is not how most companies became successful. Hardware players like Nvidia or Apple started with a product that worked and was deployable, and then they added complexity over time.”

In 2025, after his previous humanoid startup was sold to 1X, Mai (pictured above, left) teamed up with Parsa Bakhtiari (pictured above, right), a former Tesla Model 3 engineer who at one point reported directly to Elon Musk, to build what the duo hopes will become the Android of robotics.

That vision was attractive to Gradient Ventures, which backed Feather at its inception, leading the startup’s previously announced $7.6 million pre-seed round.

Since then, Feather has rolled out a modular robotic system that allows developers to customize the hardware for different use cases, such as adjusting arm lengths. The startup has already begun selling to customers, surpassing $1 million in revenue.

Although Feather is not disclosing its customers, it said that its robots are working as cooks in restaurants and cleaning up science labs. On the software side, the hardware can run models from any leading robotics AI provider, including Nvidia, Skild, or Physical Intelligence.

“We’ve been selling small quantities of these robots, and now that we resolved like almost all the issues over the last year of field testing, we’re getting ready for a big product launch,” Mai said.

According to Darian Shirazi, general partner at Gradient, Feather doesn’t have direct competitors in the U.S. He breaks down the current hardware robotics landscape into three categories: startups like Sunday building domestic household robots, heavyweights like Figure and Tesla aiming for general-purpose machines, and Feather, which, he believes, is the only U.S. startup developing a modular humanoid platform.

Mai admits that Feather took a page from Chinese robotics companies like Unitree. But with new foreign-made models restricted from entering the U.S. market, Feather is now uniquely positioned as a homegrown option of its kind.

Feather’s other advantage is its price. The robot costs $30,000, which is about half the price Unitree’s H2 Edu.

Shirazi believes the market size at that price could be very large. “You would hire a laborer for $50,000 to $60,000 a year, you’d have to train [them]. They’d have to have HR. They’d have to have all these different support mechanisms,” he said. “You can now buy a Feather robot to do that.”

Feather is also operating extremely efficiently, having spent only a fraction of its pre-seed funding, according to Shirazi.

The startup’s big bet, of course, is that the value in robotics will come from an ecosystem developed around the hardware.

“If we think about the market size today for physical AI companies, it’s very small,” Mai said. “But if you think about how many physical AI application companies will probably exist in five years, we expect it to be in the thousands.”

Feather hopes to be the platform that powers all of them.

items.title: Robots make combat airdrops, clear mines as Ukraine defeats Russian pincer
items.summary: Ukraine’s Operation Vivaldi has erased Russian gains with the help of robots.
items.content:
Ukraine’s military robots are dropping from heavy drones in airborne assaults behind Russian lines as other robots clear mines ahead of advancing Ukrainian infantry. The wheeled ground robots are supporting Ukraine’s Operation Vivaldi counterattack that has crushed a Russian military pincer movement and liberated dozens of square miles of occupied Ukrainian territory so far.

The Ukrainian Third Army Corps revealed a “world-first” airborne assault involving robots and drones that took place within Russian-held territory on September 21, 2026, according to the Ukrainian government media platform United24 . Heavy bomber drones air-dropped explosive ground robots more than six miles behind Russian frontlines, helping the robots bypass tough terrain and enemy defenses to attack supply lines in the rear.

This is not the first time that Ukraine has used heavy drones to deliver robots closer to their intended targets. But the incident is reportedly the most ambitious robotic airborne assault to date.

Several days later, the Ukrainian defense media outlet Militarnyi reported that the Third Army Corps had separately used more ground robots to safely clear antipersonnel mines from more than 18 miles of routes, paving the way for Ukrainian infantry assaults. The same task would have typically required two sapper companies—but in this case, the robots took care of it all on their own without putting human lives at risk.

Such remote-controlled robots and their human operators already take care of about 60 percent of mines in the Third Army Corps’ area of operations, according to Militarnyi and follow-up coverage by United24 .

The Ukrainian military has been significantly ramping up the use of ground robots to compensate for its manpower disadvantage against the Russian military. With the persistent threat of drone attacks near the front lines, robots are taking on increasingly risky duties such as doing supply runs or evacuating wounded soldiers.

Ukraine’s military robots are also taking on combat duties such as defending against Russian attacks with machine guns or making explosive kamikaze assaults on Russian positions.

The latest battlefield uses of such robots have helped the Ukrainian military’s Operation Vivald reclaim up to 96 square miles of territory. Operation Vivaldi has also defeated Russian forces that were the northern part of a pincer movement attempting to encircle Ukraine’s “Fortress Belt” cities in eastern Ukraine, according to the Institute for the Study of War (ISW), a think bank based in Washington, DC.

Since launching in May 2026, the Ukrainian Third Army Corps operation has practiced strict operational security that has kept successful advances under wraps for a long time. That has helped mislead Russian leaders, whose operational awareness is also hindered by what the ISW described as a “pervasive culture of lying within the Russian military” about the real battlefield situation when things aren’t going well for Russia.

Operation Vivaldi’s success has also been enabled by Ukraine’s intermediate-range drone strike campaign targeting Russian fuel supplies, which has reduced the availability of diesel fuel for generators powering Russian electronic warfare systems. At the same time, Ukraine’s own electronic warfare systems reportedly neutralized about 20,000 Russian drones.

Together, such factors have helped Ukraine achieve “tactical drone overmatch” while supporting Ukrainian mechanized advances toward Lyman in Ukraine’s Donetsk Oblast, according to the ISW assessment. Members of Russia’s elite drone unit, called Rubicon, were withdrawn from the region after the Ukrainian Third Army Corps inflicted losses on the Russian drone pilots and the unit’s resources, according to The Kyiv Independent .

But the Russian military is still directing armored vehicles and drone units such as Rubicon toward Dobropillya in the Donetsk Oblast in preparation for future mechanized assaults this autumn. During the summer, the Russian military tested a new anti-drone protection system for its most modern tanks that saw limited success—although Ukrainian drones still overwhelmed the tanks’ defenses .

The Russian military has also adapted many of the same drone warfare innovations used by Ukraine while sometimes developing its own as it continues attacking Ukrainian cities with missiles and drones. Russia has also stepped up a campaign of “hybrid warfare” against Europe, with recent examples including an explosive drone boat turning up near a vital offshore gas site and an attempt to attack parked Ukrainian cargo aircraft with a drone at Leipzig Airport in Germany.

items.title: AI-powered fuzzing with the GitHub Security Lab Taskflow Agent
items.summary: In this blog post, I explain how to use the new fuzzing taskflow based on the GitHub Security Lab Taskflow Agent AI framework. The post AI-powered fuzzing with the GitHub Security Lab Taskflow Agent appeared first on The GitHub Blog .
items.content:
If you’re new to fuzzing and want to learn the fundamentals first, check out our Fuzzing 101 course at gh.io/fuzzing101 .

Continuous fuzzing is not a magic solution that solves all your problems . Even projects that have been enrolled in OSS-Fuzz for years can still hide critical bugs, and the reason is almost always the same: someone needs to keep an eye on coverage, write new harnesses for the code that nobody is reaching, and triage the crashes that come out the other end. In other words, fuzzing still needs a human in the loop.

So the natural question I kept asking myself was: how much of that human work can we actually hand over to an LLM agent?

That is what led me to build the Fuzzing Taskflow, an autonomous fuzzing pipeline for C/C++ projects. You only need to point it at a GitHub repository, and it does the rest: it identifies the suitable entrypoints, analyzes the build system, writes the harnesses, runs AFL++, reads the coverage reports, improves the harnesses, triages every crash, and writes a vulnerability report for each unique bug, all without a human babysitting it.

The Fuzzing Taskflow is built on top of the GitHub Security Lab Taskflow Agent , our framework for writing LLM-driven security automation, so the pipeline is expressed as a set of taskflows that an agent runs end to end.

In this post, I’ll walk you through how it works and the design decisions behind it. Let’s get going!

The simplest way to run it’s just to go to https://github.com/GitHubSecurityLab/seclab-taskflows-fuzzing and start a codespace.

Then, run the script like this:

That’s it. The argument is just a GitHub owner/repo slug. Then, the agent, takes care of all the preliminary steps on its own:

If you just want a quick smoke test before committing to a long campaign, point it at something small:

A word of warning before you run it: this taskflow runs afl-fuzz , clang , and arbitrary build commands chosen by the LLM directly on the host, with no container in between. A prompt-injected agent could, in principle, do anything your user can. So please run it only inside a disposable environment (e.g., a Codespace or a throwaway VM), without elevated privileges .

Some frontier models impose security guardrails on their outputs. For the fuzzing task flow, we use Claude Sonnet 5 by default because it passed all of our internal tests without issues. You can choose a different model by modifying the following file: src/seclab_taskflows_fuzzing/configs/model_config.yaml .

Before getting into the interesting parts, it helps to know how the pieces fit together. There are three layers:

The design rule I cared about most is a clean separation of responsibility: the LLM agent owns the decisions, and the MCP tools own the execution . The agent decides what to fuzz, what harness to write, and what coverage gap to chase next. The tools just expose primitives like run_afl_for or compile_harness . The agent never calls AFL or clang directly; it composes the pipeline out of these building blocks. All the state lives in a SQLite database ( fuzz_context.db ), so the stages never hand data to each other in memory, only through the database.

One small but important detail: each harness is built twice. AFL’s edge instrumentation is great for guiding the fuzzer but useless for human-readable coverage reports. So every harness becomes both a .afl binary (built with afl-clang-lto -fsanitize=address,undefined ) and a .cov binary (built with clang -fprofile-instr-generate -fcoverage-mapping ). The .afl binary does the fuzzing; the .cov binary replays AFL’s queue afterwards to produce real source-line and branch coverage.

This is the heart of the whole pipeline, and it’s the part that most directly automates the manual workflow I described at the start.

If you have ever tried to improve fuzzing coverage by hand, you’ll know that it’s an iterative process that looks like this:

The “check the coverage” step used to be completed by me, manually reading an LCOV report looking for uncovered branches. The “improve the coverage” step was also completed by me, this time, writing a new harness or crafting a new input. The Fuzzing Taskflow hands both of those steps to the agent.

Each iteration, for each harness, the agent runs AFL for a time budget, replays the queue against the .cov binary to get a real coverage report, and then reads the list of uncovered branches. Based on what it finds, it picks one of a handful of actions:

The time budgets double every iteration:

30s → 60s → 120s → 240s → 480s → 960s (≈ 32 min/target)

The idea is to spend cheap, short rounds early (when there’s lots of low-hanging coverage to grab) and longer rounds later (when the fuzzer needs more time to break through a hard guard).

And just like in my manual workflow, I need an answer to the question: when do we stop? Here, the loop uses plateau detection : once two consecutive iterations each gain less than a configurable threshold (1% absolute line coverage by default), the loop decides it has hit diminishing returns and moves on. This keeps the agent from burning hours of compute squeezing out the last fraction of a percent.

AFL’s default byte-level mutators (bit flips, arithmetic, block splicing) do a great job on binary formats but struggle with structured, text-based inputs. The classic solution is to hand-write custom mutators for each format, which is tedious work. This time I want the pipeline to do that work for me, so it ships four complementary mechanisms for producing structure-aware inputs.

items.title: Jensen Huang talks about AI and climate change like a supervillain
items.summary: As Jensen Huang puts it, AI can help fight climate change - but only if it inflicts "an enormous amount of pain and suffering" first. The Nvidia CEO discussed the future of energy and AI's impact on our planet in the latest episode of The Ezra Klein Show. But his comments boil do
items.content:
With AI, he says, ‘in order to save you, they’ve got to hurt you first.‘

As Jensen Huang puts it, AI can help fight climate change — but only if it inflicts “an enormous amount of pain and suffering” first.

The Nvidia CEO discussed the future of energy and AI’s impact on our planet in the latest episode of The Ezra Klein Show . But his comments boil down to the same accelerationist spin we’ve seen from a variety of tech leaders as well as President Donald Trump. They promise that AI will be such a gift to humanity that it’s worth the damage caused by data centers currently running on dirty energy.

Huang’s extreme level of privilege is glaring

Huang’s extreme level of privilege is glaring in the interview. He’s right that there will be pain. People are already suffering from fires and floods exacerbated by climate change. People are already dying earlier because of air pollution from fossil fuels. But Huang, with a net worth of around $192.6 billion, will not pay the price of the pollution his company creates through energy-hungry chip factories and data centers .

Huang tells Klein, after complaining that the US hasn’t built out enough fossil fuel plants, that:

It’s kind of like, in order to save you, they’ve got to hurt you first — that’s the nature of surgery. They’ve got to cut you open to save you. They’ve got to inflict an enormous amount of pain and suffering on you so that they can save you. And so I think AI’s kind of like that.

That’s the bit that gives Thanos energy . Resources are too limited and so after disappearing half of humanity, the Marvel supervillain believes, things will be much rosier. (“I will shred this universe down to its last atom, and then create a new one, teeming with life that knows not what it has lost but only what it has been given,” he tells the Avengers.)

Huang goes on to say:

Over the next several years we have to unfortunately use fossil fuels, because we just don’t have enough sustainable energy to make a difference. And then after that, hopefully, we can transition to that.

For context, nearly every country on Earth agreed to limit climate change when they adopted the Paris agreement in 2015. The accord sets a goal of cutting greenhouse gas emissions in half by 2030 and reaching net zero around 2050. That can only happen with swift transition to carbon-free energy like renewables and nuclear. Here’s just a short list of terrible things getting worse when we stall that progress to pursue advances in AI:

These effects are showing up in Huang’s backyard, even if he’s insulated from them. He mentions in the interview that he doesn’t know what his own address is. However, he reportedly bought a $7.5 million home on Maui in 2004 — before wildfires devastated the island in 2023. That year, an Nvidia spokesperson confirmed with The Verge that the Huangs “have owned the same home in Maui for many years.”

Huang’s property reportedly escaped damage , and the Nvidia spokesperson told me that the Huangs “donated significantly to local relief efforts.” But despite the philanthropy from tech billionaires with residences on Maui, the inferno also inflamed tensions over luxury properties’ hold on Maui’s water supply .

“Billionaires coming to Maui, buying up large swaths of land as their, I don’t know, seventh vacation home, it’s painful for our community,” Maui County Councilmember Keani Rawlins-Fernandez told me at the time . “It underscores the stark disparity between Indigenous people who want to mālama ‘āina, care for our land, and those who see Hawaii as a vacation destination.”

“Billionaires coming to Maui, buying up large swaths of land as their, I don’t know, seventh vacation home, it’s painful for our community.”

While greenhouse gas pollution from fossil fuels makes wildfires more dangerous by exacerbating hot, dry conditions, climate change isn’t entirely to blame for the flames that razed much of Lahaina on Maui. I reported at the time that previous generations of wealthy land grabbers primed the islands to burn . The US annexed the Kingdom of Hawaii in 1898, egged on by American plantation owners who wanted to evade import taxes . They cleared native vegetation for their businesses, allowing invasive grasses to take hold and make the landscape much more flammable than it used to be.

So when I hear Huang make the case now that there will need to be sacrifices in the name of AI progress, it reminds me that we’ve seen this playbook before. An industry that wants to grow at any cost. And nearby communities and their descendants are just supposed to live with the aftermath.

Huang mentions growing community opposition to data centers in the interview with Klein, and scolds other companies for not spreading the good news with residents about how efficient data centers purportedly are before they start construction. “If they don’t want data centers to be built in their town or whatever it is, then so be it. But if you’re going to build in their town, be sure to go there and let them know what’s coming,” he says.

“I am inevitable,” Thanos notoriously said — and apparently, so are AI data centers.

Even so, data centers don’t actually have to be as polluting as they are turning out to be.

In the interview, Huang also (unfairly) attributes record renewable energy purchases to AI. He blames climate action for stalling the construction of energy infrastructure, presumably for fossil fuels.

I think we just have to acknowledge that we got ourselves really gummed up in climate change and sustainable energy, and as a result, we just didn’t plan enough energy production.

Then he proclaims that AI is “the best opportunity we have” to “turn a corner on climate change, if you want a future that’s sustainable.” He sees AI accelerating demand for clean energy in the long term. But AI already needs a lot of energy now, and fossil fuels are what we’ve got.

“A more polluting AI buildout is not inevitable.”

items.title: Meta is going to let you build games with AI right on your phone
items.summary: Meta has a new plan to get people to make games for its Horizon social platform. The company today announced two new development tools that will let you create games with AI prompts: Horizon Create, a mobile app, and Horizon Studio, a browser app that offers more granular control
items.content:
The next push for Meta’s Horizon platform involves AI-generated video games.

Horizon has struggled as a platform, but Meta has a plan to give these new Horizon games significantly more reach: It’s going to let published games made with Horizon Create and Horizon Studio get recommended on Facebook and Instagram, where they also will be playable.

“Someone scrolling through Instagram can tap a clip of your game and be in a multiplayer session within seconds, without needing to download an app or being redirected,” Meta says. “Your game lives natively in the feeds where people already discover content and connect with friends.” Games that are “engaging, stable, culturally relevant, and keep players coming back” will get more reach, according to the company.

The company’s announcement comes as Roblox, a similar platform to Horizon that is vastly more popular, is also making a significant push into AI-powered development, including a feature in its mobile app that similarly allows users to generate games with a prompt .

Meta’s news about Horizon, which launched as a VR app, follows a recent pivot to primarily focus on mobile . With Meta stuffing AI into basically everything it can, it’s perhaps no surprise that AI is becoming a big part of Horizon as well.

Giving people the tools to quickly make those could give people more options for things to play. I’m pretty skeptical that a bunch of AI-generated games will be as engaging as a handcrafted experience, but the games made in Create and Studio sound as if they’ll at least have the elements of video games (unlike Google’s Project Genie, which can create brief but empty AI-generated interactive experiences ). “Both enable creators to turn any idea into a complete 2D or 3D mobile game, complete with progression systems, balanced difficulty, art direction, multiplayer, and more, then refine every element to their standards,” Meta says in a blog post.

Meta also likely has a very long way to go to reach the scale of Roblox, which has 123 million daily active users. Horizon, by contrast, hasn’t ever really taken off; The Verge reported in early 2022 that it hit 300,000 monthly users.

items.title: Meta’s Muse Charm looks like a Tamagotchi, but it’s tapping into a much newer trend
items.summary: Meta’s new AI gadget may look like a Tamagotchi, but its dangling form factor taps into a much broader Gen Z trend around bag charms, retro tech, and turning gadgets into fashion accessories.
items.content:
Is Meta’s just-announced Muse Charm a playful device that will make AI more approachable to everyday consumers, or will it be yet another flop in a long list of AI hardware gadgets that didn’t take off, like the Ai Pin, Rabbit, or Friend pendant? Reactions, so far, have been mixed. What the Charm is, however, is on-trend.

Like it or not, the form factor could potentially appeal to Gen Z consumers who, in this post- Labubu era, have already been into various dangling items from keychains and bags. It’s all part of a broader kitschy, retro-inspired shift in their approach to fashion and technology.

Already, Gen Z has created a market for things that dangle, with everything from lip glosses to hand sanitizers to sunblocks to fragrances and more turned into bag charms , primarily targeted at women.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by Kristina Rodulfo (@kristinarodulfo)

Hailey Bieber’s viral Rhode lip case, which stuck the lip gloss onto a phone case , had a big influence on this idea that beauty products could also be fashion accessories, as did its other beauty-focused bag charms . (The brand saw $212 million in annual net sales from a lineup of roughly 10 products, Vogue noted last year, as the company announced its billion-dollar exit to Elf Beauty.)

Then there was the Labubu craze , which saw sales of the so-ugly-it’s-cute fuzzy monster bag charm explode, growing Pop Mart’s (the Chinese retailer behind the product) revenue to $1.8 billion in 2024 , a 7x jump from 2019. While demand for the Labubu itself has since faded, the concept of the decorative bag charm has not. One analyst firm estimates the global bag charm market will grow to over $1 billion by 2030 .

Today, bag charms can be characters, bedazzled beauty products, or other whimsical designs or objects, like Coach’s coveted cherry charms , a Gen Z favorite . They’ve proven popular because they’re a means of expressing your personality, just as humans have done for ages through their fashion choices, makeup, and jewelry.

Similarly, Meta’s Muse is a customizable character; you design your own avatar, which makes the AI agent a reflection of you, too.

And, as many have pointed out, Muse Charm’s form factor recalls a Tamagotchi, the pocket-sized digital virtual pet that became a major toy fad in the late 90s and again in the mid-2000s.

However, the Tamagotchi is not the most current reference. It seems the Muse Charm is actually a twist on what some young people are already doing with their Apple Watch. Often meant as a way to repurpose an older device , the concept of the Apple Watch keychain or charm has been growing in popularity, fueled by TikTok videos showing different ways to use the watch when not on your wrist.

never even used it for years! About to use it everyday now 🤓 #applewatch #applewatchhacks #applewatchtips #apple #lvwallet

On retailers like Amazon and Walmart, and marketplaces like eBay and Etsy , there are thousands of Apple Watch keychains, straps, pendants, lanyards, clips, and bag charm cases now available in nearly every style you can think of. As you might expect, these keychain watches are often being adopted by younger women as a fashion accessory first, rather than a piece of technology.

I’m obsessed 💕 #applewatch #teacher #teachersoftiktok #girly #cute

This all then intersects with the broader retro-tech trend , which has seen older tech like digital cameras, flip phones, iPods, CDs , cassette tapes, home phones , and wired earbuds making a quiet comeback.

This vibe shift in tech comes as young people describe the addictive, algorithm-driven feeds and “soulness” nature of technology as making them feel more disconnected, which has also fed into this trend of wanting tech they can touch and feel. (One startup, Clicks, is even bringing back the physical phone keyboard in a BlackBerry-inspired device , for instance.)

For Gen Z, these physical objects help them feel more connected with the technology they’re using and offer a sense of control over a world where technology has become so deeply integrated into our lives that it no longer feels like a choice to use it.

Young women , again, have been at the forefront of this trend, with some even crafting their own portable, mini computers, “cyberdecks, ” which they fit inside clamshell purses or custom cases, and bedazzle with jewels, flowers, stickers, pearls, and other items to make them feel more personal.

That brings us back to the Muse Charm. While it’s clearly designed with the tech-as-fashion-accessory trend in mind, that doesn’t mean it will be a hit.

Meta has abused consumer trust over the years to such an extent that it may never fully recover.

To name just a few examples: The tech giant had to settle with the FTC over charges that it deceived consumers by making users’ private information public without their consent, and has been penalized by the FTC for numerous privacy-related violations. In 2023, the FTC charged Meta with violating a privacy order that was filed after the 2019 settlement. It’s also been repeatedly hauled before Congress over its harms to minors, has lost or settled multiple lawsuits over the same topics, and has seen various whistleblowers outing its abuses.

These careless privacy practices could ultimately see Meta lose the battle to be the consumer AI of choice… unless, of course, consumers decide that the “devil you know” is better than the one you don’t. (Especially when the latter are those warning AI could put an end to the human race .)

Meta’s end game, after all, is highly-targeted, highly-personalized ads. If that’s the privacy tradeoff in gaining access to free AI — Meta said it will monetize Muse by taking a small fee from transactions — consumers could be willing to take the risk.
